title: Measure sound speed
target: Analyze sound travel measurements and their limitations.
criteria: Calculate speed from distance and time.
Use repeated measurements and discuss timing uncertainty.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A microphone and speaker are together 42 m from a wall. What path length does a reflected pulse travel back to the microphone?
cpa.guide: An echo travels to the wall and back, two equal legs.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Two synchronized sensors are 36 m apart along a sound path. A pulse travels directly from the first to the second. Which distance belongs in v = d/t?
cpa.guide: This is one-way timing between different sensors, not an out-and-back echo.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A wall is 68 m away. A pulse returns in 0.40 s. What measured sound speed follows?
cpa.guide: Round-trip distance is 136 m. v = 136/0.40 = 340 m/s.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A pulse covers 45 m one way in 0.15 s. What is its measured speed?
cpa.guide: v = 45/0.15 = 300 m/s; do not double a one-way path.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Echo times vary slightly across trials at the same distance. What is a useful response?
options: Repeat consistently and report the spread alongside the estimate.
Conclude the wall moves without other evidence.
Keep only the time closest to the expected value.
cpa.guide: Repeated data help quantify variation; selecting a preferred reading biases the estimate.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: A measured echo time is too large because of a timing delay. The distance is correct. What bias results in v = 2d/t?
options: The calculated speed is too low.
The calculated speed is too high.
The distance automatically doubles to compensate.
cpa.guide: An overestimated denominator reduces the computed speed.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.
